output.title: The real limit of dual running
output.body:
Dual running looks simple until you make it a real workflow choice. For a small business, it means keeping the manual process in place while a new AI-assisted path runs beside it. That only makes sense for one repeatable task where you are already deciding between more manual labour, another hire, or automation.

The limit is overlap. While both paths exist, someone still has to check outputs, resolve differences, and decide which path is the source of truth. For money movement or other high-risk decisions, human approval stays mandatory. That is not a nice-to-have; it is the rule.

Bareni’s normal sequence is to identify one recurring workflow, say honestly whether AI fits, and if it does, define pilot scope, fixed price, and measures. That is method, not a promise of results. Dual running is useful only while the owner can justify the extra attention it takes.

A practical next step is to ask yourself: how much owner time goes into this workflow each week, and how many decision points genuinely need your judgment? If the answer is many, dual running is probably too expensive to keep open for long. If it is narrow, a short pilot can show whether the new path is worth keeping.
